name: @argszero/cordis-plugin-session-event-guard
description: Diagnoses, at the write boundary, the three session-log mistakes an external plugin cannot see from where it stands. The first is a session event outside this harness's generated vocabulary: Session.append builds and freezes the envelope itself and cannot set `ignorable`, so such an event is REQUIRED, and the storage read path refuses the whole log later — in a different process, for every reader that does not load the writing plugin. The second is a message whose `source` still uses the anonymous `kind: 'plugin'` wrapper that session format V4 retired: it is refused synchronously at the physical row boundary with one sentence that names no event, no sequence and no plugin. The plugin judges a type and a `source` before either is written, audits stored sessions through the same validated read seam a restart uses and quotes the reader's refusal verbatim, observes live session/event writes so each mistake is reported where it is made, and builds the envelope the public handle seam accepts. It also shadows each session's append and refuses a payload no reader would accept — a message whose content is not a parts array, say — before it lands, quoting the reader's own sentence. It never writes to a session log: it refuses a write rather than performing one.
